design_detail: Prospective postpartum screening study (self-described 'sequential case series'): telephone EPDS screening at 4–6 weeks postpartum, SCID diagnostic home visits for screen-positive women; descriptive proportions and chi-square comparisons only
severity_measure: No adjustment; descriptive proportions only (EPDS used for screening cut points, not as a confounder)
comparison_group: None for main estimates (descriptive); screen-negative women only for demographic comparisons
population: Postpartum women who delivered at an urban academic hospital (Magee-Womens, Pittsburgh), screened with EPDS at 4–6 weeks; screen-positive (EPDS >=10) subset evaluated
sample_size_detail: 17,601 approached; 10,000 screened; 1,396 screen-positive (EPDS >=10; base for self-harm ideation estimate); 826 completed SCID home visits (base for onset-timing and diagnosis estimates); 147 telephone MDD-only interviews; 476 home-visited women with EPDS >=13
rationale: Descriptive screening/diagnostic study with no adjusted comparisons. Authors call it a 'sequential case series', but it reports prevalence-type estimates from a screened cohort, so coded descriptive. N is the 826 SCID-assessed screen-positive women behind the diagnosis and onset estimates that drive the conclusions.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort (planned secondary analysis of a prospective cohort), single academic center (Northwestern, Chicago); pre- vs post-implementation of perinatal collaborative care model, no concurrent unexposed control; propensity-score covariate adjustment with race-by-epoch interaction terms
severity_measure: PS covariates: maternal age, insurance, parity, tobacco, substance use history, chronic medical problem, mental health history (presence only); no severity measure
comparison_group: Pre-implementation epoch (deliveries 2015–2016); White individuals as referent for race contrasts
population: Black or White pregnant/postpartum people receiving prenatal care at Northwestern Medicine academic obstetric practices, deliveries Sept 2015–Sept 2016 and Sept 2017–Jan 2019
sample_size_detail: Pre-implementation 2,286 (262 Black, 2,024 White); post-implementation 2,424 (313 Black, 2,111 White). Secondary outcome (treatment recommendation) restricted to positive screens: pre 17 Black/9 White, post 41 Black/89 White
rationale: Pre/post epoch comparison without a concurrent unexposed control, so not quasi-experimental per protocol. PS adjustment includes only presence of mental health history. Primary outcome (antenatal screening) modeled in all 4,710 individuals.

design_detail: Population-based descriptive series of pregnancy-associated self-harm deaths (suicide and overdose), Colorado 2004–2012; vital records plus coroner, prenatal and delivery record abstraction; mortality ratios per live births and crude contextual comparison with all live births
severity_measure: No adjustment; descriptive frequencies and crude contextual comparison only
comparison_group: None for case characteristics; all Colorado women with live births (N=614,154) for demographic context
population: Women with pregnancy-associated deaths from suicide or drug overdose (during pregnancy or within 1 year postpartum), Colorado, 2004–2012
sample_size_detail: 211 maternal deaths; 63 (30%) from self-harm (used for mortality ratios per live births); detailed records for 59 (31 accidental overdose, 28 suicide); toxicology for 50; prenatal records for 48; live-birth comparison population 614,154
rationale: Authors call it a case series. The analysis is statewide surveillance with population mortality ratios and only crude demographic context, so it was coded descriptive (code 5 precedes case series in the decision order). Detailed characteristics are based on the 59 decedents with records.

design_detail: Prospective cohort, obstetric practices in Connecticut and western Massachusetts 2005–2009; Cox regression with time-dependent, 2-month-lagged antidepressant exposure; adjusted hazard ratios
severity_measure: Number of lifetime depressive episodes (1/2/3/>=4), depressive onset before age 14, number of prior hospitalizations for depression, major depressive episode in 6 months before pregnancy
comparison_group: Women with a history of depression not using antidepressants (time-varying exposure)
population: Pregnant women (<17 weeks at enrollment) with a history of depressive disorder, recruited from 137 obstetric practices/clinics in Connecticut and western Massachusetts, followed through 8 weeks postpartum
sample_size_detail: Analytic sample 778 of 2,793 interviewed (9,525 screened); 130 used antidepressants during follow-up (112 one agent, 16 two, 2 three); 123 developed a major depressive episode; 617 completed all interviews
rationale: Non-randomized comparison with Cox models adjusted for prior episodes, age of onset, and psychiatric hospitalization, which the authors call 'correlates of severe depressive illness'. No sibling analysis.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort nested in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2010 (46 states + DC); exposure in last 90 days of pregnancy; restricted to women with depression; propensity-score and high-dimensional PS fine stratification; logistic regression
severity_measure: PS included 'proxies for depression severity' (number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses), plus other psychotropic use, comorbidity and healthcare utilization; hdPS added 200 empirical covariates
comparison_group: Pregnant women with depression without antidepressant use during pregnancy
population: Medicaid-enrolled pregnant women with live-born infants, 2000–2010, restricted to those with a depression diagnosis
sample_size_detail: Source cohort 3,789,330 pregnancies (102,179 SSRI, 26,771 non-SSRI, 3,660,380 unexposed). Depression-restricted analytic cohort 739,114 = 65,316 SSRI + 16,283 non-SSRI + 657,515 unexposed (SSRI-vs-unexposed contrast 722,831; non-SSRI contrast 673,798)
rationale: Main estimate is the depression-restricted, hdPS-stratified OR (SSRI 1.10). The PS explicitly includes depression-severity proxies (counts of inpatient and outpatient depression diagnoses). No sibling or within-mother analysis is reported.

design_detail: Secondary analysis of 2 prospective observational cohorts (Pittsburgh and Cleveland, 2000–2011); Finnegan exams at 2–4 weeks by blinded raters; chi-square group comparisons plus multivariable logistic regression adjusting for preterm birth, maternal race and age
severity_measure: Logistic model adjusted for preterm birth, race and age only; SIGH-ADS depression scores compared descriptively but not entered in the outcome model; mood-disorder group defined by diagnosis alone
comparison_group: Infants of women with untreated mood disorder (n=94) and of women with neither mood disorder nor psychotropics (n=79)
population: Infants of pregnant women with MDD or bipolar disorder (SRI-treated or untreated) and unexposed comparison women, Cleveland OH and Pittsburgh PA, 2000–2011
sample_size_detail: SRI-exposed 41, untreated mood disorder 94, comparison 79; adjusted model results reported as P values only ('results not shown')
rationale: The primary comparison is crude (chi-square), but the authors report an adjusted logistic model (preterm birth, race, age) for the main exposure contrast. Per Amendments 1–2 it is coded on the adjusted estimate, which includes no severity measure.

design_detail: Single-center, 6-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of sertraline (50–200 mg/day) after a 1-week single-blind placebo lead-in; Yale, recruitment 1994–2004
population: Women aged 18–45 with major depression onset within 3 months of delivery (HAM-D 18–31), New Haven/southern Connecticut
sample_size_detail: 38 entered placebo lead-in; 2 removed for >30% HAM-D drop; 36 randomized/ITT (17 sertraline, 19 placebo); 33 evaluable; 27 met strict DSM-IV 4-week-onset criterion (ITT subgroup)
rationale: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; the primary analysis compares response rates in the 36-woman ITT sample.

design_detail: Systematic review and network meta-analysis (random effects, credible intervals) of randomized trials of drug treatments for generalised anxiety disorder; PROSPERO CRD42018087106
population: Adult outpatients with generalised anxiety disorder (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 89 randomized trials; 25,441 patients randomised to 22 active drugs or placebo; 1,992 potential studies screened
rationale: Network meta-analysis restricted to randomized trials in adult outpatients with GAD; no perinatal population.

design_detail: Two-stage design: a literature review of 8 cohort studies generated hypotheses, then a population-based case–malformed-control study in the EUROCAT Antiepileptic Study Database (19 registries, 1995–2005) tested them; logistic regression adjusted for maternal age, birth year and reporting registry
severity_measure: Adjusted for maternal age, year of birth and registry only; authors state no data on epilepsy type, seizure frequency, folic acid or dose
comparison_group: No first-trimester AED exposure (also valproic acid and other AED monotherapy); controls are non-chromosomal and chromosomal malformation registrations
population: Registrations of major congenital malformations (live births, fetal deaths >=20 weeks, terminations) in 19 European population-based registries, 1995–2005
sample_size_detail: Case-control dataset 93,436 registrations = 11,790 cases (5 malformation subgroups; spina bifida n=2,048) + 69,883 non-chromosomal controls + 11,763 chromosomal controls; 131 CBZ-monotherapy-exposed registrations; source 98,075 malformation registrations among 3,881,592 births. Literature-review component: 8 cohorts, 2,680 CBZ-exposed pregnancies
rationale: The review only generated hypotheses. The tested estimates (e.g., spina bifida OR 2.6) come from the adjusted case-control analysis, so the paper is coded observational adjusted. Authors could not adjust for 'type of epilepsy, frequency of seizures'.

design_detail: Retrospective population-based drug-utilization cohort (MEPREP: 11 US health plans including Tennessee Medicaid), 2001–2007; descriptive prevalence and trends of prenatal antipsychotic dispensing by year, trimester and diagnosis
comparison_group: None (descriptive); characteristics of unexposed deliveries shown for context
population: Live-born deliveries to women aged 15–45 continuously enrolled with pharmacy benefits in 11 US health plans, 2001–2007
sample_size_detail: 4,223 atypical-antipsychotic-exposed and 548 typical-exposed deliveries (60 days pre-pregnancy through delivery); 514,782 with no antipsychotic use; 68,946 typical-exposed when prochlorperazine/promethazine included
rationale: Purely descriptive drug-utilization study of prevalence and trends; no effect estimate or confounder adjustment.

design_detail: Prospective observational cohort (Pittsburgh, 2006–2011); repeated-measures mixed models of BSID-II scores at 12, 26 and 52 weeks. Model I unadjusted; Model II adds SIGH-ADS and MRS scores; Model III adds maternal age, education and marital status
severity_measure: Maternal symptom-severity scores: SIGH-ADS (Hamilton depression) and Mania Rating Scale entered in Models II and III
comparison_group: Infants of women with untreated bipolar disorder (BD-, n=27) and unexposed controls without bipolar disorder or psychotropics (n=116)
population: Mother-infant dyads: pregnant women with DSM-IV bipolar disorder (psychotropic-treated or untreated) and comparison women, Pittsburgh PA, 2006–2011
sample_size_detail: BD+ 54, BD- 27, unexposed 116; 52-week retention 52% (BD+), 74% (BD-), 83% (unexposed); per-time-point assessments range 16–106
rationale: Fully adjusted models include SIGH-ADS and MRS symptom scores, which count as severity. The abstract's Motor Quality finding comes from unadjusted Model I and became non-significant after adjustment (P=.0529).

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (MOOSE/PRISMA) of metabolic syndrome prevalence in severe mental illness, with relative-risk meta-analyses vs matched general-population controls and meta-regression
comparison_group: Between diagnostic groups (schizophrenia, bipolar, MDD); antipsychotic-naive participants; matched general-population controls
population: Adults with schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders, bipolar disorder or major depressive disorder (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 198 studies, 52,678 unique persons with SMI (study n 14–3,568); 29 population-based studies n=18,594; general-population comparison 6,610 SMI vs 101,223 controls. Full text in the file is the Spanish edition (World Psychiatry Ed Esp)
rationale: Meta-analysis of observational studies in adults with SMI; not perinatal. Inclusion criteria specify observational studies; RCT baseline data were also eligible but used cross-sectionally, so components coded 'Observational only'.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort nested in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2007; first-trimester exposure; restricted to depression diagnosis; propensity-score fine stratification (100 strata), hdPS confirmatory analysis
severity_measure: PS included 'proxies for depression severity' (number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses), other psychotropic use, comorbidity markers
comparison_group: Pregnant women with depression without first-trimester antidepressant exposure
population: Medicaid-enrolled pregnant women with live-born infants, 46 states + DC, 2000–2007, restricted to women with depression
sample_size_detail: Source cohort 949,504 pregnancies (64,389 antidepressant-exposed incl. 46,144 SSRI; 885,115 unexposed). Main SSRI estimate in depression-restricted PS-stratified cohort: 36,778 SSRI + 180,564 unexposed = 217,342. Other classes compared with the same unexposed group; total across all classes not reported
rationale: The fully adjusted, depression-restricted PS analysis explicitly controls depression-severity proxies (abstract: PS used 'to control for depression severity'). Robust variance for repeat pregnancies is not a within-mother analysis.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2007, restricted to women with depression; GEE relative risks with multivariable adjustment; hdPS and active-comparator sensitivity analyses
severity_measure: Number of outpatient (0, 1, 2–4, 5–9, >=10) and inpatient (0, 1, >=2) depression diagnoses, termed 'proxies of depression severity'
comparison_group: Pregnant women with depression and no antidepressant dispensing (SSRI monotherapy as active comparator in secondary analysis)
population: Medicaid-enrolled pregnant women with depression diagnoses and live births, 2000–2007
sample_size_detail: Depression cohort 100,942; 15,175 with first-trimester-only exposure excluded, leaving 85,767 in the primary analysis: unexposed 59,219; SSRI 19,000; SNRI 1,216; tricyclic 441; bupropion 2,622; other 647; polytherapy 2,622. Source population 1,248,875 pregnancies
rationale: Fully adjusted RRs include depression-severity proxies within a depression-restricted cohort. Robust variance accounts for multiple pregnancies; there is no sibling or within-mother contrast.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Kaiser Permanente Washington EHR linked to Washington birth records, 2001–2014; prior antidepressant users, continuers vs discontinuers; GEE with inverse probability of treatment weighting
severity_measure: IPTW included psychotherapy and psychiatry visits, inpatient psychiatric hospitalization, psychotropic fills and mental health diagnoses; authors: 'including mental health conditions and indicators of mental health severity'. PHQ-9 described but not modeled
comparison_group: Women with an antidepressant fill in the 6 months before pregnancy but none during pregnancy (discontinuers)
population: Singleton live births 2001–2014 to KPWA-enrolled women aged 15–45 without pre-existing diabetes who filled an antidepressant within 6 months before pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 1,634 continuers, 1,211 discontinuers; about 4% excluded from regression for missing covariates (exact analytic N not reported); blood-glucose subanalysis 1,101 births (613/488); 7% of women contributed >1 birth
rationale: Active-comparator (continuer vs discontinuer) design with IPTW on mental-health utilization and hospitalization, which the authors explicitly call severity indicators. GEE handles repeat births; there is no within-mother contrast. The exact complete-case N is not reported.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2007, restricted to women with mood/anxiety disorder diagnoses; GEE relative risks with multivariable adjustment; hdPS sensitivity analysis
severity_measure: Number of outpatient (0, 1, 2–5, 6–9, >=10) and inpatient (0, 1, >=2) mood/anxiety diagnoses, termed 'proxies of mood/anxiety disorder severity'
comparison_group: Women with mood/anxiety disorders and no antidepressant supply in the 5 months before delivery
population: Medicaid-enrolled pregnant women aged 12–55 with mood or anxiety disorder diagnoses and live births, 2000–2007
sample_size_detail: Mood/anxiety subcohort 106,000; 3,278 polytherapy excluded, leaving 102,722: unexposed 69,044; SRI monotherapy 29,222 (current 12,710, recent 6,096, past 10,416); non-SRI monotherapy 4,456 (current 1,495, recent 829, past 2,132). Source population 2,759,414 pregnancies
rationale: Fully adjusted RRs include severity proxies (counts of inpatient and outpatient mood/anxiety diagnoses) in a diagnosis-restricted cohort. Robust variances handle repeat pregnancies only; there is no within-mother contrast.
